## Design

### 2026-10-11 – ![Screenshot 2026-10-11 192816](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/odWDnpjaUyEyrgoKgv9Ah7NcXQwl2aoN/fbcd63a33f14ddecc0f2b2d588190044c1199bb6a01bfd7ec237925d144e771f.png)

**4.5h**

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 192816](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/odWDnpjaUyEyrgoKgv9Ah7NcXQwl2aoN/fbcd63a33f14ddecc0f2b2d588190044c1199bb6a01bfd7ec237925d144e771f.png)              Designed the dual-mode flying car schematic in KiCad. Integrated an ESP32 for wireless control, an MPU-6050 gyro for flight stability, an L293D chip for 2 car wheels, and 4 AO3400A MOSFETs for drone propellers. Wired an EN pull-up resistor to prevent boot loops, fixed a regulator ground short, and finalized the circuit logic blueprint.

### 2026-10-11 – Converted the schematic blueprint into the PCB layout editor. Resolved 8 compilation footprint errors by assigning standard Terminal Blocks to motor/battery inputs and through-hole dimensions to the r

**3h**

Converted the schematic blueprint into the PCB layout editor. Resolved 8 compilation footprint errors by assigning standard Terminal Blocks to motor/battery inputs and through-hole dimensions to the resistor. Spread out the component cluster, chose a compact rectangle board strategy, centered the gyro, and placed the ESP32 antenna at the edge.

### 2026-10-11 – • Set up custom trace widths: thick 1.0mm paths for +BATT, GND, and motor outputs to handle current spikes, and thin 0.25mm for data. Used a clean orthogonal layer strategy, drawing vertical lines on

**3h**

• Set up custom trace widths: thick 1.0mm paths for +BATT, GND, and motor outputs to handle current spikes, and thin 0.25mm for data. Used a clean orthogonal layer strategy, drawing vertical lines on the Front Copper (Red) layer and horizontal paths on the Bottom Copper (Blue) layer to cross tracks safely without tangling.

### 2026-10-11 – Routed all remaining long-haul control lines to the ESP32 until the unrouted counter hit zero. Selected the Edge.Cuts layer and drew the final outer rectangle boundary frame. Ran a Design Rule Check (

**3.5h**

Routed all remaining long-haul control lines to the ESP32 until the unrouted counter hit zero. Selected the Edge.Cuts layer and drew the final outer rectangle boundary frame. Ran a Design Rule Check (DRC), plotted the 10 Gerber layers, generated the drill maps, and compressed the entire package into a ZIP archive for Hack Club dashboard submission
